hits.author: auroraxo
hits.title: Add signerd to Developer Tools
hits.body:
## What's being added

**signerd** (https://github.com/auroraxo/signerd) — a scoped signing daemon for Solana that applies the ssh-agent pattern to Solana keys. AI agents hold time- and spend-bounded grants instead of private keys; the daemon checks each transaction against the grant offline before signing and refuses anything it cannot decide from the transaction bytes with a machine-readable reason.

## Why it fits the guidelines

- **Related to AI and Solana development**: designed so an agent can be told "you may send up to 0.5 SOL for 24 hours" without receiving the key — a prompt-injected agent hits a structured refusal instead of a silent gap. The README's primary example is agent key custody (contrasted with `solana-agent-kit`'s raw private key setup path).
- **Actively maintained**: first v0.1.0 released 2026-11-01, daily commits, CI green (210 tests pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped — verified locally on `main` at 5425f37).
- **Documentation available**: full README with install path, grant-file examples, and a measured safety-boundary section (offline-verifiable scope only; lookup-table/CPI transactions are refused by design).
- **Working code**: `cargo install --git ... --tag v0.1.0`, no token, MIT licensed.
- Placed next to IntentProof in Developer Tools as the closest neighbor (both are local pre-signing policy for AI-agent transactions; signerd additionally holds the key).

## Honest limits (stated in the repo itself)

- No professional security audit, no outside users yet — the README says so explicitly and asks for no real funds to use it yet.
- v1 transaction envelope remains a plan; only the legacy System-transfer scope is enforceable offline today.

Not a token project, no paid promotion.
